output.summary: KEP-5941 (DRA Shared Consumable Capacity) reached status implementable at stage alpha. The design extends shared counters with a requestPolicy on CounterSet and a valueFrom mapping on device consumption, so device requests can draw from shared capacity.
output.rationale:
The discussion centered on modelling shared capacity (such as a shared PCIe root or NUMA zone pool) in DRA. Reviewers considered alternatives including scheduler-core shared counters and extending Partitionable counters with request policies. The approach that was converged on, per johnbelamaric, was to add requestPolicy to CounterSet and valueFrom to consumption instead of a new sharedCapacities field. The LGTM from johnbelamaric on 2026-06-16 was conditioned on follow-up edits, not on the design being redone.</rationale>
<parameter name="outcome_reason">null

alternatives.option: Make shared counters part of the scheduler core, shared across DRA and ResourceFit plugins
alternatives.why_not: Raised by dom4ha and discussed by johnbelamaric and LionelJouin, who said it seemed like a completely new KEP and quite hard to model. It was not adopted for this KEP.

alternatives.option: Extend Partitionable counters with request policy and default values in consumesCounters, as proposed by sunya-ch
alternatives.why_not: sunya-ch noted it would require changing PartitionableDevice so that Counter Value is no longer required. johnbelamaric instead proposed the CounterSet and valueFrom split, with the value-or-valueFrom relaxation.
johnbelamaric said 'I don't see why we need a new sharedCapacities' and suggested adding requestPolicy to sharedCounters instead.
Judged too granular for the scheduler. The team aligned with the consumable capacity KEP and used the existing DRA metrics.

evidence.quote: I don't see why we need a new `sharedCapacities` - we can just at `requestPolicy` to the `sharedCounters`.
yes, this captures it - I think this works for the use case and is quite flexible.
